- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; cap forecast at +3–5% above prior peak.
- If sentiment turns positive mid-horizon (e.g., >0.2 after 10–15 days), model underreacts; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 0.5–1.0% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overweights early sentiment (first 5 days) and underweights late sentiment (last 5 days); weight sentiment equally across all 18-day window for smoothing.
- If sentiment is negative and price is rising, model often ignores sentiment; if sentiment > -0.2 and price > 75, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day to align with sentiment drift.
